canonical_data: a per-user profile organised by topic and an event timeline with embedded summaries, in a relational database with vector search, buffered through a cache; raw transcripts are discarded after processing unless retention is enabled
current_repo_note: Development stopped in January 2026 with several unanswered contributions, and the maintaining organisation's readme now opens by promoting a separate project that makes no reference back to this one, so no successor is declared and the supersession rule does not apply. Every first-party hosted surface is unreachable: the homepage and cloud sign-in return not-found, the playground fails, and the documented cloud host does not resolve; only the documentation site answers. The self-hosted path is intact, which is why this is not the dormancy shape that holds other candidates. No published runtime names it as a backend; its integrations run one way from its own clients.
strengths: The memory unit is a configurable per-user profile with an event timeline rather than an undifferentiated fact pile, with worked schemas shipped so an operator decides what is worth remembering before extraction
Genuinely replaceable infrastructure: three client libraries, a broad API, a tool server, and a drop-in patch that adds memory to an existing model call, all against one self-hosted stack
Profiles and events are directly editable and deletable through the API, and raw transcripts are discarded after processing by default
weaknesses: Every first-party hosted surface the readme sends readers to is gone, including the homepage, the cloud sign-in, the playground, and the documented cloud host
Development has stopped, with no commit for eight months and no client release for longer, while the same organisation promotes a different project
Its capture surface is narrower than its client advertises: the library offers six content types but the server processes only two and rejects the rest
why_it_matters: The clearest worked example of agent memory as a configurable, editable user profile plus an event timeline over an ordinary database, rather than a similarity search over accumulated facts.
